scope: Exploratory diagnostic on already exposed pilot data; no fresh confirmation, no retraining.
hypotheses: If dose-matched unprotected updates match protection, the observed benefit may be mostly weaker functional steering.
If a first-token UNKNOWN bias matches the outcome and failure cases, the learned change is largely a refusal threshold, not improved evidence discrimination.
Protection earns further investigation only if its benefit exceeds these simpler controls; the original pilot still failed its promotion criteria.
matching_signal: Mean change of UNKNOWN first-token log odds versus all other vocabulary tokens, across all 32 calibration prompts; validation/utility never choose the dose.
interpolation: Evaluate at most one linearly interpolated dose in the first adjacent grid interval straddling the protected mean; pick smallest absolute calibration mismatch, lower dose tie.
bias_control: Add the protected mean calibration log-odds shift to the UNKNOWN logit only on the first generated token, on the unchanged base.
reproduction_gate: Publicly load each saved high-dose row artifact and exactly reproduce all 128 validation and 32 utility token trajectories; four zero-bias baseline probes also must match.
interpretation_gate: A relative calibration-matching error above 10% is an inadequate dose match; do not infer direction effects from it.
